# Map images

A map background is a pyramid of tiles (Deep Zoom, like Owlbear Rodeo's renderer), never one texture: one texture failed black above the GPU's `MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE` and forced imports down to 8192 px. Code in `src/app/pixi/mosaicCanvas/`.

- **Every map can be seen whole**: the view's zoom range is `MIN_ZOOM` to `MAX_ZOOM` (`pixi/zoomRange.ts`), and a map larger than `MIN_ZOOM` shows lowers the least zoom to the scale that fits it (`fitZoomRange` at every load, `fitMapRect`, Shift+1 through `allowZoom`), so the fit and the wheel both reach it. Anything else that needs a zoom outside the range widens it with `allowZoom` (`focusToken`).

- **Geometry** (`pyramid.ts`, pure): level 0 is the image at full size, level n `ceil(size / 2ⁿ)`, down to one tile. Tiles are 510 px of content plus 1 px of each neighbour on inner sides (512 px bitmaps), whose texture frame is the content, so bilinear filtering at a seam reads the neighbour's real pixel; no per-tile mipmaps, the pyramid is the mip chain. World units are level-0 pixels at (0, 0), as before (grid sizes, UVTT cells and `worldTexel` depend on it), unless the grid's alignment stretches the map (Map stretch, under Hexagonal Grids): `MosaicCanvas` alone applies that, and the pyramid, the tiles and the layer stay in image pixels. Place a level with its exact `scaleX` / `scaleY` (world size / level size), never `scale` (2ⁿ, for level of detail only): rounded-up levels would drift towards the far edge. `TESSERA_SPEC` names the recipe; change it with any change of tile size, overlap, quality or level rule, and cached pyramids of another spec are rebuilt.
- **Level of detail** (`levelOfDetail.ts`): the finest level whose texels cover at least half a screen pixel, so nothing is drawn minified more than 2×. The overview is the finest level whose longer side is at most 2048: always loaded while a map is shown, the first picture of a scene and the fallback under loading tiles.
- **Built once per device, kept** (`tesseraStore.ts`, `indexedDbTesseraBackend.ts`): IndexedDB `atlas-vtt-map-tiles-<appId>`, keyed by the SHA-256 of the image's bytes, with `path|size|mtime` remembered so an unchanged file is not hashed again. Never in the vault: tiles are device facts (Vault files, above), thousands per map, and every device makes the same. A manifest is `complete` only after its last batch; tiles and the manifest's byte count are written in one transaction. Eviction drops whole pyramids, least recently used, within min(2 GiB, 10 % of quota); pinned pyramids (open maps, builds) are never evicted or cleared. Settings: Map image cache (size, Clear).
- **The worker** (`tesseraWorker.ts`, one per app through `TesseraDecoderClient.forApp`, released in `onunload`): an open sends the file's identity only, and the worker asks for the bytes (`vault.readBinary`, never a resource URL) only when no complete pyramid can serve it, so a cached map opens without reading its file. Otherwise it decodes once, halves into levels (`resizeQuality: 'medium'`), answers tile requests by cropping at once and encodes lossless WebP tiles (`TESSERA_QUALITY` 1: a tile decodes to exactly the pixels it was cut from, `losslessMosaicCanvases.gpu.test.ts`; lossy tiles turned a 1 px red line grey) into the cache in the background, coarsest first, answering requests between tiles. Decoded levels share a 1 GiB budget; opens go before prebuilds, background builds give way, and an open of a shown map never waits on another shown map's build (it goes over the budget instead). Sources over 2 GiB decoded with levels (about 402 MP) are refused as `too-large`. SVG and what the worker cannot decode is decoded on the main thread (`decodeImage`) and handed over as a bitmap; its world size stays the size an `<img>` gives it. A request of a closed map rejects with `MapClosedError`, which readers take as "no image". A crashed worker is restarted, its handles die with it, and `MosaicCanvas` reopens its map in a new layer; a worker that fails before it starts leaves the core running in-thread for good.
- **`MosaicCanvas` is the one owner** of a view's map (`MapController` loads it; `PixiRendererOrchestrator.getMapImage`): `worldRect`, `layer` (viewport index 0), `overview(maxSide)` (a CPU bitmap of the whole map fit within `maxSide`, composed from the finest level at least that large), `albedoTexture()` (the overview as a mipmapped texture, for the lighting's bounce), `whenReady(rect, worldPerScreenPixel, ms)`, `addDemandRegion(view)` and `drawFor(view)`. **Never read map pixels from a texture or a display object; use `overview()`.** Readers of the map's size take `worldRect` (`getMapRect`); the fog reads it through a provider each time it computes bounds, and `'map-image-updated'` only says it changed. A change of `state.background` that no load made (undo, `mapFileFallback`, `cleanupMissingAssets`) reloads the image (`MapController`). The loading screen waits up to 1.5 s for the tiles of the camera the scene opens with, the tab's own camera included, so the crossfade reveals a sharp map. The overviews of the last three maps stay on the GPU (`ResidentOverviews`), so switching back is instant.
- **Drawing** (`MosaicCanvasLayer.ts`, `tesseraCoverage.ts`, `tesseraTextureCache.ts`): a render group with one container per level and sprites at integer level-pixel positions. Coverage is computed per view: the GM camera (checked every tick: pixi-viewport's `moveCenter` and `setZoom` emit nothing), each demand region, and a whole-map picture view at scene-card size. A wanted tile is always drawn once loaded; ancestors (up to 5 levels) and descendants (up to 2) are kept only while it is missing or fading, and a fallback ancestor covered by opaque finer tiles is hidden. Tiles fade in over `MOTION_NORMAL_MS` (none with reduced motion). Sprites are shared, but each picture shows only its own view: the canvas the GM's, while `drawFor(view)` switches for one synchronous render and must be restored before the DM's render (the player capture in `withPlayerSafeFrame`, thumbnails through `captureSceneFrame`). The player window registers the frame it renders as a demand region (`PlayerFrameDemand`) and lets go of it when it hides, holds a frame or closes. GPU tiles live in our own LRU (160 MiB, at most 4 uploads a frame, then `requestRender`); `ImageSource` forces `autoGarbageCollect` on in its constructor, so the cache turns it off after construction, or PIXI's GC would drop retained tiles and re-upload from a closed bitmap. Don't use PIXI's `Culler`. `tests/gpu/mosaicCanvasSeams.gpu.test.ts` holds tiles to the single-texture render (no seam at 100 % and 400 %), `mosaicCanvasViews.gpu.test.ts` the per-picture views.
